req.title: Task update persists
req.statement: The system shall persist PUT changes so subsequent GET requests reflect the update.

doc.reasoning: The test suite is designed to validate the persistence of task updates via the PUT /tasks/{task_id} endpoint. It includes tests for positive, negative, and boundary cases to ensure comprehensive coverage. The positive test verifies that valid updates are persisted correctly. The negative test checks that invalid updates are rejected with appropriate error responses. The boundary test ensures that updates at the edge of valid input constraints are handled correctly.

tests.name: test_update_task_positive
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send a PUT request to update the task with id 1
expected: Task is updated with new values
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Positive test: Update an existing task
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 6", "description": "Updated description", "completed": false}
)
assert response.status_code == 200
updated_task = response.json()
assert updated_task["title"] == "Read chapter 6"
assert updated_task["description"] == "Updated description"
assert updated_task["completed"] is False

tests.name: test_update_task_negative
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send a PUT request with invalid data to update the task with id 1
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Negative test: Attempt to update a task with invalid data
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "", "description": "Updated description", "completed": false}
)
assert response.status_code == 422

tests.name: test_update_task_boundary
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send a PUT request with boundary-valid data to update the task with id 1
expected: Task is updated with boundary values
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Boundary test: Update a task with boundary-valid data
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "A", "description": "X" * 500, "completed": true}
)
assert response.status_code == 200
updated_task = response.json()
assert updated_task["title"] == "A"
assert updated_task["description"] == "X" * 500
assert updated_task["completed"] is True
